To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the convergence of continuous time ELS parameter estimates is guaranteed for all stable signal models driven under bounded input conditions, provided that a coloured noise/prediction error positive real condition is satisfied.
ELS identification is globally convergent for bounded input signals, and that ELS and LS can be combined in a manner that is globally convergent.
the convergence of the ELS and LS parameter estimators is guaranteed for stable systems and that the convergence of LS parameter estimator is guaranteed for unstable systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a unified theory of continuous-time adaptive identification, which is sufficiently general to include the ELS and LS algorithms as special cases.
the development and analysis of adaptive estimation schemes for a class of linear stochastic signal models which include both stable and unstable models.
a class of adaptive estimation schemes that are well-suited for implementation on real time systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, under a coloured noise condition, the ELS identification scheme has global convergence and improved transient performance.
the theory provides a sound foundation for the design of continuous time adaptive identification and control schemes.
the ELS and LS parameter estimates converge to the true parameter values, and the ELS and/or LS identification schemes are robust to model uncertainty, bounded inputs and ill-conditioning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory presented in this paper is a major step in the direction of providing a unified framework for the analysis of continuous-time adaptive estimation algorithms.
, for both ELS and least squares (LS), the positive real condition is necessary and sufficient for almost sure convergence of the estimates to a neighbourhood of the true parameter values.
we have a global convergence theory for the continuous-time adaptive estimation of a class of stochastic signal models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ELS is a very useful tool for adaptive estimation of stochastic signal models.
the convergence theory for ELS estimation is much simpler than that for LS estimation, and the ELS theory is also more general.
ELS estimation can be made robust with respect to finite time escape, and that the resulting schemes can be used in a range of control applications, including indirect adaptive control.
